attribution.note: Marcus states both the historical existence claim and the hedged training inference in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the historical claim and training hedge. In context, existing code means the same basic functionality, not identical implementation.

contract.note: The functional-predecessor reading is ordinary and supported by the surrounding comparison. Excluding the explicitly hedged training inference from scoring is appropriate.

evidence.note: The historical repository documents implementation and installation of a photograph-to-ingredients-to-recipes application predating Roose’s essay. It does not establish training exposure.
The dated user reports corroborate public code availability before the essay. Credential and model-access failures limit usability, but do not contradict the existence of implementation code.

reviews.rationale: The repository and dated public usage reports establish a predecessor implementing the same basic photo-to-recipe idea. Reported access failures do not negate code existence. This verdict covers only the firm historical assertion; the hedged training inference is not scored or established.
